name: Chung Mong Jin
current_role: Chairman (and CEO), KCC Corporation / KCC Group, South Korea
profile: Eldest son of KCC founder Chung Sang-young (youngest brother of Hyundai founder Chung Ju-yung), he has led KCC, Korea's leading paint, building-materials and silicone maker, since the 2000s. He steered KCC's 2019 consortium buyout of US silicones maker Momentive Performance Materials from Apollo (~$3bn) and in 2024 moved KCC to full ownership.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership KCC bought Momentive Performance Materials from Apollo in 2019 for about $3.1bn, turning a Korean paint company into one of the world's largest silicone producers; in 2024 it agreed to buy out partner SJL Partners for 100% ownership.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is KCC corporate communications via the company website. Brother Chung Mong-ik is vice chairman.

name: Lady Green
current_role: Co-founder, Green & Mingarelli Design (Monaco); owner of Taveta, the former Arcadia Group parent
profile: Lady Tina Green (born Christina Stuart-Paine), wife of retailer Sir Philip Green, was the legal owner via Jersey-held Taveta of the Arcadia Group (Topshop, Dorothy Perkins, Burton), which entered administration in 2020. Monaco-based, she now runs a yacht and aircraft interior design firm with Pietro Mingarelli.
interesting_fact: Although Sir Philip Green ran Arcadia, the retail empire was legally owned by Tina Green through a Jersey company, Taveta, which held the family's shares.
deep_cut_fact: With partner Pietro Mingarelli she designed the Benetti superyacht Illusion V inside and out; her studio is known for building each yacht around a single theme (once an antique woodcarving found in a northern Thailand market) and for its 'hidden cupboards'.
notes: Very private, Monaco-resident. No published personal or office contact found. Her design firm (Green & Mingarelli Design) is the most plausible professional route but no verified site/email found.

name: Holger Timm
current_role: Chairman of the management board, Berliner Effektengesellschaft AG; CEO, Tradegate AG Wertpapierhandelsbank
profile: A Berlin stockbroker who founded Berliner Effektengesellschaft (BEG) in 1986 and remains its majority shareholder. BEG holds about 57% of Tradegate AG, which runs the Tradegate trading platform (launched 2000) and co-owns Tradegate BSX exchange with Deutsche Börse; BEG also holds a stake in Quirin Privatbank.
interesting_fact: Tradegate, launched in 2000 as one of the first electronic trading systems for German online brokers, became a full exchange (Tradegate BSX) co-owned with Deutsche Börse and is now a key venue for retail traders and neobrokers; Timm chairs its exchange council.
notes: Low media profile. BEG ownership ~56.6% of Tradegate per 2025 half-year report (Forbes' 88% figure refers to his stake in BEG). Generic company inboxes only.

name: Igor Kudryashkin
current_role: Commercial director and co-owner, Ural Mining and Metallurgical Company (UMMC); executive board member, Svyatogor
profile: Long-time commercial director of Iskander Makhmudov's UMMC, a major Russian copper, zinc, coal and gold producer, who received a UMMC stake when the business was reorganised in 2013. His family also controls a majority of European Media Group, a large Russian radio-station network.
interesting_fact: Besides metals, Kudryashkin's family holds more than two-thirds of European Media Group, whose eight radio stations reach roughly 35 million listeners a week.
notes: UK-sanctioned since Feb 2024 (listed for his Svyatogor/UMMC role, updated Apr 2025; see opensanctions.org/entities/NK-TCxUTL6L7fKzsmG7XVhB22). Not a suitable outreach target; no published contacts found.

name: Azman Hashim
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, AmBank Group; Chairman, Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers
profile: Malaysian banker (born 1939) who bought the Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank in 1982 and built it into AmBank Group (AMMB Holdings), chairing it until 2019 and retiring fully in 2022. He holds stakes in RCE Capital and Amcorp Properties and still chairs bodies including the Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers and the Malaysia-Japan Economic Association.
interesting_fact: He summited Mount Kinabalu (4,095m) on 31 October 2023 at age 84, his second ascent after first climbing it at 71 in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He passed the Senior Cambridge exam with first-class marks at 15, then trained as a chartered accountant in Perth, Australia (1955-60) on a Colombo Plan scholarship; his grandmother came from Imabari in Japan's Ehime prefecture.
notes: Retired from AmBank; best route is via the Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers (aicb.org.my) or AmBank corporate communications. Received a Chartered Banker Institute (UK) lifetime achievement award in June 2025 (Bernama). No personal contact published.

name: Evelyn Danzig Haas
profile: Bay Area philanthropist and widow of Levi Strauss & Co. chief Walter A. Haas Jr.; co-founder of the Evelyn and Walter Haas Jr. Fund. She died in February 2010, aged 92.
notes: Died Feb 2010 per AP obituary: https://www.heraldnet.com/2010/02/04/philanthropist-evelyn-haas-dies-at-age-92/ . Listing likely stale; the family's Levi Strauss stake passed to heirs.

name: Chamath Palihapitiya
current_role: Founder & CEO, Social Capital; co-host, All-In podcast
profile: Sri Lankan-born Canadian-American investor who was an AOL VP and then led Facebook's growth team (2007-11) before founding Social Capital in 2011, an early backer of Slack, Box and Groq. Social Capital became his family office in 2018; he sponsored SPACs that took Virgin Galactic, SoFi and Clover Health public and co-hosts the All-In podcast.
interesting_fact: Social Capital's 2024 annual letter (June 2025) reported $2.147bn under management from $1.4bn paid-in capital; it was an early investor in AI-chip startup Groq.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating in electrical engineering from the University of Waterloo in 1999 he started as a derivatives trader at BMO Nesbitt Burns, then moved to California in 2001 to join Winamp before becoming AOL's youngest VP, running its instant-messaging (AIM) division.
notes: Very public and media-savvy; highly active on X. Interested in energy/AI infrastructure topics (All-In regularly covers data centers and power). No public email published.

name: Geng Diangen
current_role: Founder and director (former chairman, to May 2022), Beijing Sinnet Technology (Guanghuan Xinwang, SZ:300383)
profile: Founded Beijing Sinnet Technology in 1999 and built it into one of China's major internet data center and cloud operators (it runs AWS's Beijing region cloud services); listed in Shenzhen in 2014. He stepped down as chairman in 2022 and remains a director and major shareholder. Sinnet is now building AI computing centers in Hainan and Inner Mongolia.
interesting_fact: Sinnet, the data-center company he founded, launched AI 'intelligent computing center' projects in Hainan and Inner Mongolia in 2024 and deployed inference capacity at its Tianjin cloud campus, a direct fit for a data-center podcast.
notes: Low public profile, Chinese-language media only. Aggregators (MarketScreener) say he holds a graduate degree from UT Austin, unverified in primary sources. Route via Sinnet IR.

name: Muneaki Masuda
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Culture Convenience Club (CCC), Japan
profile: Born 1951 in Hirakata, Osaka, he opened the first TSUTAYA store there in 1983 and founded Culture Convenience Club in 1985, building Japan's largest book, music and video rental/retail chain plus the T-Point (now V POINT) loyalty program. He took CCC private in 2011 and has been chairman since 2024, with Yasunori Takahashi as CEO.
interesting_fact: CCC created the T-Point loyalty card, which grew into one of Japan's largest points programs and merged with SMBC's V POINT in 2024; CCC also runs design-led bookstores such as Daikanyama T-Site.
deep_cut_fact: He named his first store, 'Tsutaya Shoten Hirakata' (1983), after 'Tsutaya', the trade name of his grandfather's family business; only later did he adopt the Edo-era publisher Tsutaya Juzaburo as a role model for TSUTAYA as a modern 'producer'.
notes: Best route is CCC's media-relations inquiry page. Japanese-language outreach likely more effective.

name: Max Turnauer
profile: Son of Constantia group founder Herbert Turnauer; inherited Constantia Industries (Fundermax, Isovolta) in the family split. Died in 2020 aged 90; his son Stanislaus Turnauer now chairs and owns the group.
notes: Death reported by Industriemagazin on 9 Nov 2020: https://industriemagazin.at/industrie/der-industrielle-max-turnauer-verstorben/ . Listing is stale; relevant living person is Stanislaus Turnauer (Constantia Industries).

name: Bernard Charles
current_role: Co-founder and former Executive Chairman, Dassault Systèmes (stepped down from board Feb 21, 2026)
profile: Breton-born engineer who joined Dassault Systèmes in 1983, ran it as CEO from 1995 to 2023 and built it into a global 3D design/PLM software leader (CATIA, SolidWorks, 3DEXPERIENCE). He became chairman in 2022 (executive chairman from 2024, when Pascal Daloz took over as CEO) and stepped down in February 2026 for personal reasons, saying he would apply his experience to AI-driven transformation of industrial production.
interesting_fact: In 1989 he initiated the 'digital mock-up', a complete virtual 3D model replacing physical prototypes, which underpinned the shift to fully digitally designed products such as aircraft. HBR ranked him the world's 13th best-performing CEO in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he earned the French 'agrégation' in mechanical engineering, the country's most senior teaching qualification, plus a PhD in automation engineering from ENS Cachan; in 1986, three years after joining, he founded Dassault Systèmes' New Technologies, Research and Strategy department.
notes: Left Dassault board Feb 2026 but 'remains available' to the company; his stated next focus is AI for industrial production ('Generative Economy'), a good podcast hook. Company contacts may not route to him personally now.

name: Zhu Wenchen
current_role: Founder/controller, Furen Pharmaceutical Group (Henan); also owns Songhe Liquor (status uncertain)
profile: Henan-based pharmaceutical entrepreneur, founder and long-time chairman of Furen Pharmaceutical Group, which took control of listed Shanghai Minfeng Industrial in 2006; he also owns Songhe Liquor. Publicity-shy; few current details available.
notes: Identity match to Forbes 'pharmaceuticals' listing is likely Furen's founder but not confirmed from Forbes. Per Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Wenchen), regulators found Furen had falsified results and banned him from the securities market for 10 years in 2020; not a recommended outreach target.

name: Silvio Scaglia
current_role: Founder, SHS A.M. (quant asset manager, 2020); owner of Freedom Holding / Pacific Global Management (Elite World Group parent)
profile: Swiss-born Italian engineer and telecom entrepreneur who launched Omnitel (Italy's second mobile operator) as CEO in 1995, then founded e.Biscom/Fastweb in 1999, the world's first all-IP fibre-to-the-home operator, selling his 18.7% stake to Swisscom in 2007. He later bought Elite World modelling agencies (2011) and La Perla (2013), and in 2020 founded AI-driven asset manager SHS.
interesting_fact: Fastweb was the first company in the world to build a fully IP-based network and the first public consumer fibre-optic network; e.Biscom's 2000 IPO was the second most successful in Italian history, and Time named him among 2003's 'tech survivors'.
deep_cut_fact: Fresh out of Turin Polytechnic (electronic engineering, cum laude, 1983) his first job was at Aeritalia Spazio, where he worked on the Tethered Satellite project with NASA and Martin Marietta, before stints at Andersen Consulting, McKinsey and Piaggio.
notes: His 'Freedom Holding' (ex-Pacific Global Management) is unrelated to Nasdaq-listed Freedom Holding Corp (Timur Turlov). Ongoing high-profile litigation with ex-wife Julia Haart over Elite World since 2022; avoid. Acquitted in the Fastweb/Telecom Italia Sparkle case (2013, upheld 2017). No published contact found.

name: Zeng Lingshan
profile: Listed with source of wealth 'Creat'; could not identify this person or confirm the company (searches for the name with Creat Group / 科瑞 returned no match).
notes: Unresolved identity. 'Creat' may refer to Beijing-based Creat Group (founded by Zheng Yuewen) or Shenzhen Colibri/Kerui Technology; neither links to this name in sources found. Needs Chinese-name verification before use.

name: Chris Oglesby
current_role: CEO and majority shareholder, Bruntwood; CEO, Bruntwood SciTech
profile: Manchester-raised property entrepreneur who joined Bruntwood, the commercial-property company his father Michael Oglesby founded in 1976, in 1991 and became CEO in 1999. He has grown it into a major owner of offices and science parks across Manchester, Liverpool, Leeds and Birmingham, including Bruntwood SciTech (Alderley Park, Manchester Science Park), a JV with Legal & General.
interesting_fact: Bruntwood donates 10% of its annual profits to charitable causes, and Oglesby is a trustee of The Oglesby Charitable Trust, which works with 40+ community charities a year.
deep_cut_fact: After studying at LSE and City University and a brief spell working in the City of London, he returned north in 1991 to join his father's firm; today he leads Greater Manchester Business Board's Clean Growth Mission and is interim chair of Innovation Greater Manchester.
notes: Accessible, civic-minded and media-friendly (appeared on Business Leader podcast, Jan 2025: https://bruntwood.co.uk/blog/in-conversation-with-business-leader-bruntwood-and-bruntwood-scitech-ceo-chris-oglesby/). Strong on clean growth / science-park infrastructure angle.
